content:
Hi everyone! My name is Leonardo Restrepo, happy to go by Leo.

I'm a PhD student in public policy at George Washington University, studying higher education and school finance. I recently took a doctoral econometrics sequence, and was captivated by both applied and theoretical econometrics in the context of discrete choice and transport models.

I've always regretted not taking more mathematics in undergrad (I stopped at ODE, linear algebra, and statistics), and have started to work my way through "The Mechanics of Proof" by Heather Macbeth and "Analysis I" by Terrence Tao as a means of developing both mathematical rigor and familiarity with Lean's syntax.

Broadly, I have three goals:

  • I want to complete Lean formalizations of the proofs in Tao and Macbeth's books as a way of growing my mathematical reasoning ability.
  • I want to be able to read and grapple with the discrete choice literature, and formalize results in lean as a personal project.
  • I want to contribute (sustainably) to any ongoing efforts in the Mathlib repo.

I wanted to politely ask about the appropriateness of an amateur like myself participating in this space, as well as the use of AI to support my own learning in the absence of formal instruction. I appreciate any insight or advice you have as I make my way through Lean, and look forward to learning more about the space!
